title: User Input / Output
subStepTitle: Things to Know in C++/Java/Python or any language
subcategory: Things to Know in C++/Java/Python or any language
problemStatement: Learn how to read input from stdin and write output to stdout correctly. Online judges treat your program as a pure function of the input stream — format mismatches cause WA even when logic is perfect.
intuition: Think of the judge as a pipe. You consume tokens in a known order and emit a deterministic answer. Types, separators, and newlines are part of the contract — not decoration.

approaches.title: Idiomatic Python I/O
approaches.idea: Use input() for simple tasks. For multi-token / larger input, prefer sys.stdin.buffer.
algorithm: Read tokens with the types the statement promises.
approaches.code:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    a = int(data[0])
    s = data[1].decode()
    print(a, s)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
approaches.space: O(total input size) if you slurp; O(1) extra if you stream
approaches.spaceNote: Slurping is fine for small tasks; stream tokens for huge input

commonMistakes: Heavy flushing on large output (TLE in C++).
patternRecognition: Every CP problem starts with an I/O contract.
n ≥ 1e5 in Python → prefer buffered reads to avoid TLE.
followUps: How do you handle 1e5 test cases efficiently in Python?
interviewInsight: Interviews rarely quiz I/O, but messy I/O fails online assessments silently. Treat samples as a contract.
